::: {.callout-note}
This site documents medfit 0.14.0. CRAN has 0.3.2, which lacks
`mediation_demo` and the native, joint and cluster functions; install from
GitHub or r-universe (see the [home page](https://data-wise.github.io/medfit/#install)).
:::

**Four steps.** By the end you will have fitted a mediation model,
read its effects, and added an interval.

1. Fit: `med()`
2. Read: `quick()`, then `nie()`, `nde()`, `te()`, `pm()`
3. Tabulate: `tidy()`
4. Add an interval: `boot = TRUE`

Then pick your model on the [Models](models.html) page.

## Step 1. Fit

`mediation_demo` is a simulated dataset that ships with the package. Its two
covariates affect both the mediator and the outcome, so every example adjusts
for them (see `?mediation_demo`).

```{r}
#| label: med-simple
library(medfit)

data(mediation_demo)

result <- med(
  data = mediation_demo,
  treatment = "treatment",
  mediator = "mediator1",
  outcome = "outcome",
  covariates = c("covariate1", "covariate2")
)
```

## Step 2. Read

One line first:

```{r}
#| label: quick
quick(result)
```

| Letters | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **NIE** | Indirect effect: through the mediator (`a * b`) |
| **NDE** | Direct effect: treatment to outcome with the mediator held fixed (`c'`) |
| **PM** | Proportion mediated: the share of the total effect that goes through the mediator |

Then each piece on its own:

```{r}
#| label: extractors
nie(result)   # indirect effect
nde(result)   # direct effect
te(result)    # total effect (indirect + direct)
pm(result)    # proportion mediated
paths(result) # a, b and c'
```

## Step 3. Tabulate

`tidy()` gives a table with standard errors; `glance()` gives one row per model.

```{r}
#| label: tidy
library(generics)

tidy(result)
glance(result)
```

Add confidence intervals, and ask for only the paths or only the effects:

```{r}
#| label: tidy-ci
tidy(result, type = "effects", conf_int = TRUE)
```

The base R generics work too: `coef()`, `vcov()`, `confint()` and `nobs()`.
`confint(result, parm = "effects")` gives delta-method intervals for the effects.

## Step 4. Add an interval

Set `boot = TRUE`. The default is the parametric bootstrap, which is fast and
assumes the estimates are approximately normal.

```{r}
#| label: med-bootstrap
result_boot <- med(
  data = mediation_demo,
  treatment = "treatment",
  mediator = "mediator1",
  outcome = "outcome",
  covariates = c("covariate1", "covariate2"),
  boot = TRUE,
  n_boot = 1000,
  seed = 42
)

quick(result_boot)
```

The nonparametric and plugin methods, and a custom statistic, are in
[Bootstrap Inference](bootstrap.html).

## Already have fitted models?

`extract_mediation()` turns `lm`, `glm`, `lmer` and lavaan fits into the same
objects, so every function above still works:

```{r}
#| label: extract-mediation
fit_m <- lm(mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2, data = mediation_demo)
fit_y <- lm(outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
            data = mediation_demo)

med_data <- extract_mediation(
  fit_m,
  model_y = fit_y,
  treatment = "treatment",
  mediator = "mediator1"
)

nie(med_data)
```

## Want more control?

`fit_mediation()` takes the two formulas and an engine, and returns the same
objects. Its paths are slots on the result:

```{r}
#| label: fit-mediation
med_data <- fit_mediation(
  formula_y = outcome ~ treatment + mediator1 + covariate1 + covariate2,
  formula_m = mediator1 ~ treatment + covariate1 + covariate2,
  data = mediation_demo,
  treatment = "treatment",
  mediator = "mediator1"
)

med_data@a_path   # treatment to mediator
med_data@b_path   # mediator to outcome
med_data@c_prime  # treatment to outcome, the direct path
```

The engine is `"glm"` by default. Others:

| Engine | Use it when | Page |
|---|---|---|
| `"glm"` | the default; continuous, binary or count variables | [Simple](model-simple.html), [glm families](model-glm-families.html) |
| `"regmedint"` | you want the closed-form regression estimator | [regmedint](model-regmedint.html) |
| `"lmer"` | the treatment is assigned to whole clusters | [Cluster-randomized trials](model-cluster.html) |
| `"native"` | a latent mediator, constraints, or a model written as syntax | [Native engine](model-native.html) |

## Where next

Pick the row that matches your data.

| I have | Read |
|---|---|
| A binary or count variable | [Binary and non-normal variables](model-glm-families.html) |
| Inverse-probability weights | [Weights and robust SEs](model-weights.html) |
| A treatment-by-mediator interaction | [Treatment-by-mediator interaction](model-interaction.html) |
| Two mediators in a chain | [Serial mediation](model-serial.html) |
| Two mediators side by side | [Parallel mediation](model-parallel.html) |
| Several mediators with products | [Joint mediation](model-joint.html) |
| A treatment given to whole clusters | [Cluster-randomized trials](model-cluster.html) |
| A `lavaan` fit | [lavaan models](model-lavaan.html) |
| Model syntax, a latent mediator, constraints, intercepts or a product term | [Native engine](model-native.html) |
| Something else, or not sure | [Models](models.html), the full list |
| An error or warning | [Troubleshooting](guide-troubleshooting.html) |
| Which interval to report | [Which interval should I use?](guide-intervals.html) |
| A term or symbol you do not know | [Glossary and symbols](guide-glossary.html) |

For quick lookups: the [Reference Card](refcard.html) has every function on one
page, and the [Cookbook](cookbook.html) has twenty-one short recipes. To understand
the classes, read the [Introduction](introduction.html); for the math behind
every effect and standard error, [Methods and Formulas](methods.html); for
extraction from fitted models, [Model Extraction](extraction.html).
